facets.answer: NVIDIA reported shipping initial Vera Rubin samples to customers in February, an actual sampling milestone. It does not establish broad or commercial-volume shipments. Management’s latest cited guidance is production shipments starting in Q3 2026, within the second half; separate claims that the platform is in production or volume production describe manufacturing progress, not confirmed customer shipments. No verified shipment count or value is provided. Supply-chain and geopolitical pressures are identified as possible schedule risks.

The evidence supports customer interest, announced plans and technical readiness, but not broad operating customer deployments. CoreWeave reported completing NVL72 bring-up and validation in June and shared measured performance results—meaningful readiness evidence, not proof that the system is operating commercially. SK Telecom’s AI factory, NAVER’s planned buildout and SpaceX’s satellite payload are prospective projects; cited operating or launch dates are in the future. The card provides no confirmation that these announced facilities or systems are already installed and operating with Vera Rubin.

No realized revenue attributable to Vera Rubin is demonstrated. The nearly $20 billion figure cited by NVIDIA is a forecast for standalone CPU revenue, not reported revenue from Vera Rubin systems or the platform as a whole. Other roughly $20 billion Vera sales claims are also guidance or expectations. The card gives no recognized Vera-related revenue or separate reporting that would verify the forecast; standalone CPU revenue should not be conflated with system revenue.
